title: State (BSES YPL) v. Ravinder
court: Addl. Sessions Judge-05 (Electricity), East, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi
result: Convicted u/s 135; theft bill (Rs. 1,73,901) settled and deposited during trial; posted for sentence
statutes: Third proviso to Section 135(1) Electricity Act 2003

interpretations.interpretation: Hooking wires from the licensee's pole (YVR J081) to unmetered premises is a clause (a) connection. 'Dishonestly' takes its s.24 IPC meaning (wrongful gain/wrongful loss).

Reverse-onus clause: proof of an artificial/unauthorised means raises a compulsory presumption of dishonest use (Neeraj Dutt) rebuttable on the prudent-man standard (Hiten P. Dalal); natural rebuttal is paid bills / lawful metered use, the s.106 Evidence Act onus lying on the consumer (Mukesh Rastogi).

citations.case: Punjab State Electricity Board v. Ashwani Kumar
citations.principle: An inspection report prepared by officers in discharge of official duty carries a presumption of regularity; onus on the consumer to rebut by cogent evidence.

citations.case: Sushil Sharma v. BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd.
citations.principle: Non-examination of an independent/public witness is no infirmity where inspecting officials are trustworthy and bear no enmity to the accused.
'Shall presume' denotes a compulsory legal presumption the court is bound to draw until the fact is disproved.

citations.case: Hiten P. Dalal v. Bratindranath Banerjee
citations.principle: Rebuttal of a statutory presumption need not be conclusive; evidence must make the defence reasonably probable to a prudent man.

citations.case: Mukesh Rastogi v. North Delhi Power Ltd.
citations.principle: Easiest rebuttal of the theft presumption is production of paid electricity bills; Section 106 Evidence Act places that onus on the consumer.

significance.point: A landlord present at the tap answers for it
significance.explanation: Premises unmetered, landlord found at the spot with the theft running; the tenant's later disappearance did not shift or dilute liability.
2.435 KW wooden-work load produced a Rs. 1,73,901 assessment at double the commercial tariff (Reg. 63).

significance.point: A filed 65B certificate forecloses the videography challenge
significance.explanation: With Ex.PW3/A on record, the fabrication suggestion had nothing to bite on.
Bare planted-wire suggestions, denied by the witness, cannot dent the presumption of regularity (Ashwani Kumar).

significance.point: Settlement plus deposit still corroborates guilt
significance.explanation: Full payment of the settled bill was treated as conduct inconsistent with innocence, not closure.

generic_facts.theft_mode: direct theft / pole hooking (yellow wire joined to two-core black wire from BSES pole)
generic_facts.premises: ground floor (back portion) of village house; partly tenanted
generic_facts.occupant_at_inspection: accused (landlord) and his tenant both present; tenant later vacated, untraceable
generic_facts.ownership_evidence: investigation + neighbours' statements established accused as landlord
key_evidence: seized half-metre wire identified in court
generic_facts.defence: bare denial/false implication; no defence evidence; settled and deposited theft bill
